findings.title: Outdated docstring — project renamed from Nightwatch to Noxaudit
findings.description: The module docstring still references 'Nightwatch' but the project was renamed to 'Noxaudit' according to CHANGELOG.md. This is misleading to new developers.
findings.suggestion: Update line 1 to: """Noxaudit: Nightly AI-powered codebase audits."""

findings.title: Report title still references 'Nightwatch' instead of 'Noxaudit'
findings.description: The generate_report function uses 'Nightwatch Report' in the markdown title, but the project was renamed to Noxaudit. This will appear in all generated reports.
findings.suggestion: Change line 8 from '# Nightwatch Report: {_focus_display(result.focus)}' to '# Noxaudit Report: {_focus_display(result.focus)}'

findings.title: README example shows old CLI command name in output
findings.description: In the 'What It Looks Like' section, the example output shows 'nightwatch: 3 new findings' but should show 'noxaudit: 3 new findings' reflecting the renamed CLI command.
findings.suggestion: Update the example output in the README to use 'noxaudit' instead of 'nightwatch'

findings.title: Missing provider-specific model configuration example
findings.description: The docstring mentions 'providers.<name>.model' in configuration but doesn't clearly document that this overrides the global 'model' setting. The README shows this feature but the config module documentation is incomplete.
findings.suggestion: Add docstring clarification showing that provider-specific models override the global model setting, with an example in get_model_for_provider()

findings.title: Documentation references code that was removed
findings.description: CONTRIBUTING.md shows 'should_run_prepass' as a dead variable fixed in #46, but looking at the actual code in runner.py, the variable 'should_run_prepass' is still in use in _maybe_prepass(). The comment is outdated or references incorrect issue number.
findings.suggestion: Verify the actual issue #46 fix and update the example to reflect current code patterns, or remove the outdated reference

findings.title: Duplicate contributing documentation
findings.description: Both CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/contributing/index.md contain nearly identical content but with slight variations. This creates maintenance burden and risk of divergence.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate the two files. Keep CONTRIBUTING.md as the source of truth and reference it from docs/contributing/index.md, or merge content and remove duplication

findings.title: Documentation shows old 'nightwatch' references in example output
findings.description: The example output in 'Step 1' shows 'my-app — security' but other sections of documentation show command names with 'noxaudit'. This is inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Ensure all example outputs consistently use current tool names and formatting

findings.title: Missing docstring on main CLI group
findings.description: The main() function has a docstring, but other CLI commands lack comprehensive docstrings explaining what they do and their use cases.
findings.suggestion: Add descriptive docstrings to run(), submit(), retrieve(), decide(), baseline(), status(), report(), and estimate() commands

findings.title: MAX_FILE_SIZE constant lacks documentation
findings.description: The constant MAX_FILE_SIZE = 50_000 is hardcoded without explanation of why this value was chosen or how it relates to token limits.
findings.suggestion: Add a comment explaining the rationale: '# ~50KB to avoid large generated files, roughly ~12K tokens'

findings.title: ContentTier enum docstring could be more detailed
findings.description: The ContentTier class docstring is minimal. It doesn't explain the use case (pre-pass triage) or how tiers map to file content enrichment.
findings.suggestion: Expand docstring to explain: 'Content tier for pre-pass classification — determines how much of a file content to send to main audit. Used by prepass.py to enrich files before main audit.'

findings.title: Test file docstring lacks context on why CLI integration tests are mandatory
findings.description: The docstring mentions the policy but doesn't reference CONTRIBUTING.md or explain the historical reason (features passing unit tests but not wired to CLI).
findings.suggestion: Enhance docstring to reference CONTRIBUTING.md and explain the policy rationale more clearly

findings.title: Missing documentation for _maybe_prepass return value
findings.description: The _maybe_prepass function returns a 3-tuple (should_run, files, message) but the docstring doesn't document what the 'message' contains or when it's empty vs populated. This affects usability.
findings.suggestion: Add docstring: 'Returns: (should_run_prepass: bool, filtered_files: list[FileContent], message: str) — message explains why prepass was auto-enabled, empty if not triggered'

findings.title: Focus prompt header references 'codebase files' but some focus areas audit beyond that
findings.description: The security prompt says 'Examine EVERY provided file' but doesn't clarify whether this includes config, infrastructure code, and edge functions — which are explicitly mentioned later.
findings.suggestion: Update opening: 'Examine EVERY provided file including config files, scripts, edge functions, and infrastructure code — do not skim'

findings.title: resolve_model_key fallback logic lacks documentation
findings.description: The function uses substring matching ('opus', 'pro', 'flash', 'nano', 'mini') to map models to pricing, but this heuristic is not documented. Users may be confused when a model they expect to map doesn't.
findings.suggestion: Add docstring explaining the heuristic: 'Falls back to substring matching in model names when exact match fails. Provider parameter disambiguates between similar names (e.g., flash in Gemini vs Anthropic)'

findings.title: File hash change detection logic not documented in filter_findings
findings.description: The filter_findings function checks file_hash to detect if file changed, but the docstring doesn't mention this behavior. Users might be surprised when a dismissed finding resurfaces after file edits.
findings.suggestion: Update docstring to document: 'File change detection: if file content hash differs from decision time, finding resurfaces even within expiry window'

findings.title: CLASSIFICATION_PROMPT uses placeholder {focus_names} that's not immediately obvious
findings.description: The prompt string has {focus_names} which gets formatted in build_classification_prompt(), but there's no docstring explaining this templating pattern.
findings.suggestion: Add comment: '# Prompt string is formatted with focus_names via build_classification_prompt()'
